claim: The filter a stereo flanger puts in front of itself and the filter a stereo chorus puts in front of itself are one section. Swept at every setting the chorus's was published at -- 15 of them across the two filter shapes the byte beside it offers -- the two types return the same skirt over a hundred and thirteen twelfth-octave bands to a median of 0.08 dB at worst, where those runs repeat themselves to 0.08 dB and where one step of the byte being swept moves the profile by at least 0.15 dB. The agreement is at the floor and the thing it is being told from is two to ten times the floor, so this is the reading saying the same section twice and not the reading running out. The page prints the two types' parameter lists identically -- same order, same addresses, same ranges -- with one entry in the flanger's that the chorus has not got, a feedback level in the slot the chorus leaves empty. That list is what made the question worth asking and it is not what answers it; what this file claims is the front end, and what the loop is around is queued. The byte the flanger has and the chorus has not is a loop, and it is around the delay the byte beside it sets. A loop around a delay has to do three things and none of them is what a filter does, so each was asked separately and the modulator was parked at no rate and no depth throughout so that the delay stood still while they were. It puts teeth in the spectrum: 23.4 decibels of them at the ends of the byte, against 0.79 dB at the centre the page prints as nought -- so the printed nought is no loop rather than a small one. It deepens them without moving them: across the three settings either side where the teeth clear the run's own repeats, the delay read off the comb does not move at all while the depth goes from a third of its range to all of it. And it spaces them by the delay the byte beside it sets, which is the one that says the loop is around that delay and not around some second structure: at pre-delay 6 the comb reads 0.618 ms and at 13 it reads 1.318, a ratio of 2.133 where the byte's own is 2.167. That is the same delay per step of the byte in both places, 0.1022 ms, read two ways that did not have to agree. The loop's sign is the cheapest confirmation of all and it is there: below the printed nought the teeth sit halfway between where they sit above it, which is what an inverting loop does and what nothing else does. Scored as an inverting comb the negative settings beat the same profile scored as an in-phase one by 1.59 times at worst, and the delay each sign returns is the other's to within the width of the reading. The run that would separate the two modulators was made and could not. What it returned is not a depth curve: on both types the excursion falls as the byte climbs at one setting or another, and the setting each was asked at twice repeats to 27.2 and 10.5 per cent. The margin this file queued the run with was a hundredth of that, because it was taken from what the stage repeats to on the records already published with it -- a part's own vibrato on a held tone, which is a different quantity from a chorus's pitch read off a struck note through a swept delay. Nothing is claimed from the comparison. What the run does say, and says clearly, is why it could not: the mean pitch of the chorus's output climbs with the depth byte by 7.31 Hz where the flanger's moves 0.51, and a symmetric sweep shifts no mean at all. A sweep driven past the delay it is sweeping around is clamped on one side, and a clamped sweep shifts the mean and stops answering to the byte -- which is both of the things this run returned. The pre-delay was parked at the setting a comb read as six tenths of a millisecond, shorter than either type's own printed default, and that is the run's own doing rather than the unit's.

measurements.why: The flanger's pre-filter through the low pass, with the loop opened, the modulator parked and the balance at all-effect.
The chorus's, published earlier, on the same grid at the same settings.
The flanger's through the high pass, which is the second shape the byte beside the cutoff offers and a different skirt to agree on.
The chorus's through the high pass.

The flanger's rate byte. Carried for the one setting where the two records disagree, and not as evidence that they are one structure -- the rate table is shared by nineteen types and cannot say anything about two of them in particular.
The chorus's rate byte, whose setting-32 reading rests on two of four takes and lands off the grid the rate class closed on.

document_rows.why: Both parameter lists in full, because the claim's second sentence is about them and a reader has to be able to see that the difference is one row. They are evidence about a page and nothing else; the section is read off the skirts.

era_priors.claim: A chorus and a flanger on a fixed-point part of this period are the same arithmetic: a short modulated delay summed with the dry signal, with the flanger differing by a path from the delay's output back to its input. Writing them as two stages costs two copies of the interpolator and the modulator for one extra multiply-accumulate of difference.
era_priors.why: It says why one front end being shared is worth reading as the two types being one stage rather than as two stages that happen to filter alike. It carries none of the claim: what is claimed is the section the measurement reached.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The two front ends had differed. They did not, at fifteen settings across two filter shapes, by more than the runs repeat themselves.

adds: Each record says what one type's pre-filter byte does to a band profile. What is read out of the pair is that the two profiles are the same profile -- a comparison between records, made against a third figure neither record states, which is what one step of the swept byte is worth under the same reading.

through the low pass.where_the_widest_figures_sit: Every one of them below about forty hertz, which is the bottom of the band set and where a held note has least energy to put in a band. The medians are taken over all of it and are two orders under the widest.

through the high pass.where_the_widest_figures_sit: Every one of them below about forty hertz, which is the bottom of the band set and where a held note has least energy to put in a band. The medians are taken over all of it and are two orders under the widest.

the_rate_byte_on_both.why_this_is_not_evidence_here: One table serves nineteen types, which is a closed claim of this archive's own. Two types returning the same entry of a table that every type returns entries of says nothing about those two being one structure, and it is set down here because leaving it out would look like it had been avoided.
the_rate_byte_on_both.what_it_is_good_for: A ruler. At setting 32 the two records disagree by 7.3 per cent, which is the one figure in this file that does not agree -- and the chorus's reading there rests on two of its four takes, with a third of them returning the flanger's value exactly. The rate table's own step settles it without another run: where that step is a twentieth of a hertz the flanger's 1.65 lands 0.0 steps off an entry and the chorus's 1.7799 lands 0.4 off the nearest one there is. A reading off the grid the class already closed on is a misread, not a second table -- and at the other three settings both types land within 0.03 of a step of an entry, each measured against the step its own region of the table has.

what_the_two_runs_held_differently: The flanger's run held `40 03 08` at 64, which is the centre of a range printed `-98% - +98%` and is the loop opened. The chorus has no such address, so there was nothing to match; the comparison is of a flanger with no feedback against a chorus.

The flanger's run held `40 03 09` Phase at 0 and the chorus's run left it where the unit powers it up. Both runs held the modulator's depth at 0, so there was no modulation for a phase between two modulators to be a phase of.

alternatives.reading: Two separate filter sections written from one specification, rather than one section reached from two types.

separated_by.sensitivity_here: Not applicable. The two readings predict the same output at every setting of every byte, so no sensitivity would help.
separated_by.why_not_separable: Nothing leaving this unit's sockets distinguishes one routine called from two places from two routines computing the same numbers. The archive can say the responses are the same, which it does; what it cannot say is how many times the coefficients are stored. The era prior leans one way and a prior may not close a claim.

alternatives.reading: The two types share a front end and nothing else -- the same pre-filter bolted to two different delay lines and two different modulators.

separated_by.observable: The modulation depth of both types read as a pitch excursion at the same settings of `40 03 07` Depth and `40 03 06` Rate, with the flanger's `40 03 08` at 64 so its loop is open. A flanger with no feedback and a chorus are the same arithmetic if the delay line and the modulator are shared, so the excursion in cents either matches at every depth setting or it does not.

predicts.one stage reached twice: The same excursion at every depth setting, to the vibrato reading's own repeats.
predicts.a shared front end only: Excursions that differ at some depth setting by more than one step of the depth byte is worth.

separated_by.divergence: One step of the depth byte, which on the types already read this way is several per cent of the excursion.
separated_by.sensitivity_here: 27.2 per cent, which is what this stage repeated an excursion to on this stimulus when the run was made. The figure this entry carried before -- a few parts in a thousand -- was measured on a part's own vibrato over a held tone and does not transfer to a chorus's pitch read off a struck note.

run.stimulus: a held tone with the pre-delay at or above each type's own printed default, so that the deepest setting of the depth byte still has delay beneath it to sweep into. The first attempt parked it at six tenths of a millisecond and the sweep clamped.

separated_by.what_the_first_attempt_returned: Excursions that fall as the byte climbs on both types and repeat to 27.2 per cent, with the chorus's mean pitch climbing 7.31 Hz across the byte. Published and read out of as nothing.

alternatives.reading: The flanger's extra parameter is a loop around the same delay line the chorus uses. Answered in half: it is a loop, and it is around the delay this type's own pre-delay byte sets. That the chorus reads from that same line is not measured and is recorded as what is still open rather than as what was shown.

separated_by.observable: The decay of the flanger's response at several settings of `40 03 08`, with the modulator parked so the delay is fixed. A loop around a delay of d milliseconds puts its resonances at multiples of 1/d and makes them sharper as the byte goes up; the pre-delay byte then moves those resonances by exactly what it moves the delay by, which is what says the loop is around that delay rather than around something else.

predicts.a loop around the shared delay: A comb whose spacing is one over the pre-delay setting, moving with the pre-delay byte and sharpening with the feedback byte.
predicts.a second structure of its own: Resonances that do not move with the pre-delay byte, or do not space themselves by it.

separated_by.divergence: The whole spacing of a comb, which at a pre-delay of a few milliseconds is hundreds of hertz.
separated_by.sensitivity_here: A twelfth-octave band set separates 0.0847 octaves, which at the frequencies a comb of this spacing puts its teeth is far finer than one tooth.

run.stimulus: the same held note, modulator parked, pre-delay asked at two values so the comb has to move

alternatives.ruled_out_by: Not ruled out -- carried, and then narrowed. The run made all three readings a loop owes: teeth twenty-three decibels deep where the printed nought gives under one, a delay that does not move while the byte deepens them, and a spacing that follows the pre-delay byte to 1.6 per cent. The sign flip is there as well. What it did not read is the chorus's delay, so the word the alternative turns on -- shared -- is the part left open.

alternatives.reading: The loop is around a delay of its own that happens to track the pre-delay byte, rather than around the delay that byte sets.

separated_by.observable: Nothing this rig can reach. A delay of its own that follows the same byte returns the same comb at every setting of it, and a comb is the only thing the output can be asked.

predicts.one delay in a loop: teeth at multiples of one over the byte's delay

separated_by.sensitivity_here: 1.6 per cent, which is how closely the spacing already follows the byte.
separated_by.why_not_separable: It is the same shape of alternative the archive already carries for a table reached twice: two structures with the same arithmetic are one structure as far as an output goes. What the agreement does rule out is a loop around something the pre-delay byte does not move, which is what it was asked.

refuted_by: The two pre-filters departing at a setting neither run asked -- the grid is eleven of a hundred and twenty-eight through the low pass and four through the high pass, so a table that agreed at those and not between them would look exactly like this. Or either type's filter turning out to move with something the other's does not: both runs parked the modulator and opened the loop, and a pre-filter that depended on either would have been read at one point of a surface rather than as a curve.
what_it_would_change: Two of the sixty-four types stop being two front ends. One pre-filter section, one byte choosing between off, a low pass and a high pass, and one cutoff table, serve both -- and the cutoff table is the one the frequency class already closed.

It puts the question where it belongs. If the front ends are one section then what separates a chorus from a flanger on this unit is whatever the feedback byte reaches, and that is one run rather than a comparison of two whole types.
what_this_does_not_settle: The delay line. Nothing here read one: both runs parked the modulator and the pre-delay, which is what makes the filter comparison clean and is also what takes the delay out of it.
Whether the front end is one section or two identical ones. No reading of this unit's output can tell those apart and the first alternative says so.

Whether the delay the loop is around is the one the chorus reads from. The loop and the delay it is around are measured; that the chorus shares that line is not, and a chorus has no loop to read a comb with. The delay byte read on both types by a route that does not need feedback is what would answer it.

What the pre-delay byte's table is. Two of its settings are now measured in milliseconds, 0.618 and 1.318, by a route no other reading here uses -- the spacing of a comb. Two points are not a table and the page prints the range as 0 to 100 ms, which neither of them is near.

The modulator. It has now been asked once and the run clamped its own sweep, so the two types' depth bytes are measured and neither curve is a reading of its byte. The question is unchanged and the run to make is named beside the alternative.

what_the_feedback_byte_is_around.what: A loop from the delay's output back to its input, around the delay the pre-delay byte sets. Read as a comb rather than as a peak: the profile is scored against every delay from a tenth of a millisecond to ten, by how much more it holds at that delay's multiples than between them, and the same profile is scored against the opposite sign as the control.

put_teeth_in_the_spectrum.why_the_nought_matters: Every profile in both records is taken against that setting, so a loop still running there would subtract itself out of all of them. It is not running: the widest band of either record at that setting is under a decibel, where the byte at its ends moves twenty-three.

spaced_them_by_the_byte_beside_it.why_this_is_the_one_that_settles_it: Teeth at multiples of one over something say there is a delay in a loop. Teeth that halve their spacing when a particular byte doubles say it is that byte's delay. Nothing else in this type moves a comb that way, and a second delay of the loop's own would not move at all.

and_the_loop_inverts_below_the_nought.why_it_is_worth_asking: An inverting loop resonates at the odd half-multiples where a positive one resonates at the multiples, so its teeth land exactly between the other's. No filter, no second delay and no amount of anything else moves a comb by half a spacing and leaves it a comb. It is the cheapest confirmation available that what is being read is a loop, and it cost four of the run's twenty settings.

what_the_feedback_byte_is_around.what_this_does_not_reach: Whether the delay it loops around is the one the chorus reads from. This says the loop is around the delay `40 03 05` sets on this type, and `40 03 05` is a row both parameter lists print -- but the chorus's pre-delay was never read as a comb, because a chorus has no loop to read one with. What would answer it is the delay byte on both types measured by a route that does not need feedback.

the_run_that_could_not_answer.what: The depth byte read as a pitch excursion on both types, at six settings, with the flanger's loop held open. Published because the takes are honest and the numbers are what the unit returned; read out of here as nothing about either modulator.
the_run_that_could_not_answer.what_the_alternative_assumed: A few parts in a thousand, taken from the vibrato records already published -- a part-level vibrato on a held tone. The bar was right for that stimulus and wrong for this one, which is the same error as quoting a bound as a property, made one step earlier: in the queue entry rather than in the reading.

how_the_two_types_compare.why_it_is_not_read: Against a repeat of 27.2 per cent, three of these ratios would clear the bar. They are not read, because a curve that falls as its own byte climbs is not a measurement of that byte, and both curves do that. A comparison between two quantities neither of which is being measured is not evidence either way.

the_run_that_could_not_answer.what_would_answer_it: The same run with the pre-delay well up -- at or above each type's own printed default rather than at the six tenths of a millisecond a comb was read at -- so that the deepest setting of the byte still has delay underneath it to sweep into. Ten minutes. Whether the excursions then match is the question this file is named after, and it is still open.
